note: The single source for presentation VALUES. Edit this file, then run design/generate_tokens.py; ios/WingFoilKit/Sources/WingFoilKit/Presentation/DesignTokens.swift, web/css/tokens.css and web/js/tokens.js are generated from it and CI fails on drift (design/check_tokens.py --check).
colorNote: Every colour carries BOTH forms because the two platforms speak different languages: `hex` is what the web renders, `swiftUI` is the semantic system colour the iOS app asks for (which adapts to light/dark and to the accessibility settings, and is therefore NOT the same literal RGB as `hex`). Each platform consumes its native form; the pair is the token.
rampNote: `swiftUI: "literal"` is the one exception, and only the `speed` ramp uses it: a ramp's job is to be ORDERED and interpolable, and the semantic palette is not ordered — systemPink renders as a red on iOS, which would put the ladder's fell-in ink at the fast end of a speed ramp. So the ramp's stops are the authored RGB on both platforms, chosen mid-tone so every one of them reads on a near-white card and a near-black one, and deliberately clear of the outcome ladder (green / amber / red / grey) and of the clean-jibe mint.

flew.means: flew through — carried the maneuver on the foil

courseChange.means: bear-away / round-up — a non-verdict, deliberately outside the ladder

splash.means: the barometer saw the wrist go under

failedTakeoff.means: the one effort-layer event with an outcome, so it alone borrows the ladder's red

window.means: the selected record window: the glow on the track and the shading in the chart (the `effort` layer's ink, hex = systemOrange on dark)

flying.means: track tinted on foil (hex = systemTeal on dark, what SwiftUI .teal renders as)

offFoil.means: track tinted off foil (hex = the secondary label over a dark surface, what SwiftUI .secondary renders as)

ink.means: chevron ink — subordinate to every marker, so ink plus opacity, no hue

port.means: port ENTRY tack — a side, never a verdict, so deliberately outside the ladder

starboard.means: starboard ENTRY tack — the same hue at a second lightness, plus a dashed stroke

jibe.means: clean jibe — the strict verdict's own ink: a green deliberately NOT the ladder's flew-through green, because clean is what a jibe cost and flew through is how it ended

stopped.means: ramp stop 1 of 5 — a standstill. The cold end: an indigo blue, the one hue nothing else on the turn page uses

slow.means: ramp stop 2 of 5 — well under the speed he came in at

entry.means: ramp stop 3 of 5 — THE ANCHOR: the speed the turn was entered at, and deliberately the same value as phase.flying, so 'he held his entry speed' is drawn in the ink the app already means flying with

fast.means: ramp stop 4 of 5 — above the entry speed. Past the anchor the ramp leaves the cool half, because a rider who accelerated through a turn should be able to see it at a glance

fastest.means: ramp stop 5 of 5 — the hot end, 1.3x the entry speed and up. A magenta, not the amber or the red: those are outcome words, and a fast vertex is not a verdict

takeoffFree.means: hollow up-arrow — the wind did it

takeoffFailed.means: hollow red u-turn — went at it and came back down

cleanJibe.means: filled star — a clean jibe, drawn instead of that turn's outcome dot
